nodes.name: Schur's triangularization theorem
nodes.statement: For every matrix $T\in M_n(\mathbb{C}),$ there is a unitary matrix $U\in M_n(\mathbb{C})$ such that $U^{-1}TU$ is an upper-triangular matrix.
assumptions: $T\in M_n(\mathbb{C}),$
conclusions: there is a unitary matrix $U\in M_n(\mathbb{C})$ such that $U^{-1}TU$ is an upper-triangular matrix
nodes.statement_short: Every complex square matrix is unitarily similar to an upper-triangular matrix.

nodes.name: Normal plus nilpotent decomposition of matrices
nodes.statement: Alternatively, there exists a basis in $\mathbb{C}^n$ such that the matrix of the operator $T$ with respect to this basis is upper-triangular. Taking the diagonal part $N$ of the operator $T$ in this basis, we obtain a normal operator. The difference $T-N$ is, obviously, a strictly upper-triangular matrix. Every strictly upper-triangular matrix is, clearly, nilpotent. Thus, an arbitrary matrix is a sum of a normal matrix and nilpotent matrix.
nodes.statement_short: From Schur's theorem, every matrix is the sum of a normal (diagonal) and a nilpotent (strictly upper-triangular) matrix.

nodes.name: Quasinilpotent operator
nodes.statement: Recall that an operator $Q$ is quasinilpotent if its spectrum is $\{0\}$ and that, by the C$^*$--property, the functional calculus for self-adjoint operators and the spectral radius formula (see~\cite{KR1}), for an operator $Q$ on Hilbert space we have \[ \|\big((Q^*)^nQ^n\big)^{1/2n}\|_\infty=\|(Q^*)^nQ^n\|_\infty^{1/2n}=\|Q^n\|_\infty^{1/n} \] and quasinilpotency of $Q$ is equivalent to \begin{equation} \lim_{n\to\infty}\|\big((Q^*)^nQ^n)^{1/2n}\|_{\infty}=0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $Q$ is quasinilpotent if its spectrum is $\{0\}$, equivalently $\|((Q^*)^nQ^n)^{1/2n}\|_\infty\to0$.

nodes.name: Norm characterization of quasinilpotency
nodes.statement: \lim_{n\to\infty}\|\big((Q^*)^nQ^n)^{1/2n}\|_{\infty}=0.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3

nodes.name: Extension of Haagerup-Schultz to diffuse finite von Neumann algebras
nodes.statement: In the above theorem, the hypothesis that $\mathcal{M}$ be a II$_1$--factor and $\tau$ its tracial state can clearly be loosened to require only that $\mathcal{M}$ be a diffuse, finite von Neumann algebra and $\tau$ be any normal, faithful, tracial state on it. This is because (a) any such $\mathcal{M}$ can be embedded, via a normal, trace-preserving $*$-homomorphism, into a II$_1$--factor (to see this, use for example Lemma~2.3 and Theorem~2.5 from~\cite{D94} to see that the free product with respect to traces of $\mathcal{M}$ with $L^\infty[0,1]$ is a II$_1$-factor) and (b) the projection onto a hyperinvariant subspace of any operator belongs to the von Neumann algebra generated by the operator (this is easy to show, but for a proof see, for example, Proposition~ 2.1 of~\cite{D05}).
nodes.statement_short: The Haagerup-Schultz theorem holds in any diffuse finite von Neumann algebra, by embedding into a II$_1$-factor.

nodes.name: s.o.t.-quasinilpotent operator
nodes.statement: We note that the quasinilpotent operator in Ringrose's theorem is here replaced by an s.o.t.-quasinilpotent operator, which is an operator $Q$ such that $((Q^*)^nQ^n)^{1/2n}$ converges in strong operator topology to $0$; in this notation (which was introduced in~\cite{DFS}) s.o.t.\ is an abbreviation for ``strong operator topology;'' that quasinilpotent operators must be s.o.t.--quasinilpotent follows from the characterization~\eqref{eq:Q*nQn} of quasinilpotency.
differentia: $((Q^*)^nQ^n)^{1/2n}$ converges in strong operator topology to $0$
also_stated_at: We call such operators s.o.t.-quasinilpotent (this notation was introduced in \cite{DFS}).
nodes.statement_short: $Q$ is s.o.t.-quasinilpotent if $((Q^*)^nQ^n)^{1/2n}\to0$ strongly; quasinilpotent operators are such.

nodes.name: Haagerup-Schultz characterization of s.o.t.-quasinilpotent operators
nodes.statement: By Theorem~8.1 of~\cite{HS2}, in a finite von Neumann algebra the s.o.t.-quasinilpotent operators are precisely those whose Brown measures are concentrated at $\{0\}$.
also_stated_at: Thus, an operator $T$ has Brown measure supported on $\{0\}$ if and only if $((T^*)^nT^n)^{1/2n}$ converges in strong operator topology to $0.$
assumptions: in a finite von Neumann algebra
conclusions: the s.o.t.-quasinilpotent operators are precisely those whose Brown measures are concentrated at $\{0\}$

nodes.name: Decomposition theorem (normal plus s.o.t.-quasinilpotent)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a diffuse, finite von Neumann algebra with normal, faithful, tracial state $\tau$ and let $T\in\mathcal{M}$. Then there exist $N,Q\in\mathcal{M}$ such that \begin{enumerate}[{\rm (a)}] \item $T=N+Q$, \item the operator $N$ is normal and the Brown measure of $N$ equals that of $T$, \item the operator $Q$ is s.o.t-quasinilpotent. \end{enumerate}
assumptions: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a diffuse, finite von Neumann algebra with normal, faithful, tracial state $\tau$ and let $T\in\mathcal{M}$.
conclusions: the operator $N$ is normal and the Brown measure of $N$ equals that of $T$,
nodes.statement_short: Every operator in a diffuse finite von Neumann algebra is a normal operator with the same Brown measure plus an s.o.t.-quasinilpotent operator.

nodes.name: Triangular structure of the decomposition
nodes.statement: As in Ringrose's theorem, a family $(q_t)_{0\le t\le 1}$ of $T$--invariant (in fact, $T$--hyper\-in\-vari\-ant) projections is involved in Theorem~\ref{decomposition}, and $N$ and $Q$ can be regarded as diagonal and upper triangular, respectively, with respect to this family of projections. Indeed, $N$ is obtained as the conditional expectation of $T$ onto the von Neumann algebra generated by $\{q_t\mid 0\le t\le 1\}$. However, unlike in Ringrose's theorem, the dimensions (i.e., in our finite von Neumann algebra setting, the traces) of the projections $q_t$ can take large jumps as $t$ varies. Indeed, if $T$ itself is s.o.t.-quasinilpotent, then our construction yields $N=0$ and $\{q_t\mid 0\le t\le 1\}\subseteq\{0,1\}$.
nodes.statement_short: $N$ and $Q$ are diagonal and upper triangular w.r.t. a hyperinvariant nest $q_t$; $N$ is a conditional expectation of $T$, but the nest may have large jumps.

nodes.statement: Let $T\in B(H)$ be a compact operator and let $\Phi$ be a real--valued increasing function on $[0,\infty)$ such that $\Phi(0)=0$ and $\Phi\circ\exp$ is convex. Then $$\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\Phi(|\lambda(k,T)|)\leq\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\Phi(\mu(k,T)).$$

Then $${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{A}}(T)=\lim_{n\to\infty}{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{A}_n}(T),\quad(T\in\mathcal{M}),$$ where the limit is taken in the strong operator topology.

nodes.statement_short: Conditional expectations onto a monotone sequence of subalgebras converge strongly to the expectation onto the limit algebra.
nodes.label: exp limit lemma

nodes.name: Peano-curve construction of the nest $q_t$ and algebras $\mathcal{D}$, $\mathcal{D}_n$
nodes.statement: Let $T\in\mathcal{M}$ and let $\rho:[0,1]\to\{|z|\leq \|T\|_{\infty}\}$ be a Peano curve.\footnote{A continuous surjective mapping $[0,1]\to[0,1]^2$ was first constructed by Peano \cite{Peano}. See, for example, \cite{Man} for details. We may take the ball rather than the square since they are homeomorphic.} \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item Set $q_t$ to be the Haagerup--Schultz projection for $T$ associated to the Borel set $\rho([0,t]).$ Then $q_t$ is increasing in $t$. Since $\tau(q_t)=\nu_T(\rho([0,t])$, we have $q_t=\wedge_{t'>t}q_{t'}$; i.e., $q_t$ is strong-operator-topology continuous from the right in $t$. \item Set $\mathcal{D}$ to be the von Neumann algebra generated by $\{q_t\mid t\in[0,1]\}.$ \item For every $n\geq0,$ set $\mathcal{D}_n$ to be the algebra generated by $q_{k/2^n},$ $0\leq k\leq 2^n.$ \end{enumerate} For technical convenience, we will assume that the Brown measure of $T$ has no atom at $\rho(0)$ (i.e. $\nu_T(\rho(0))=0$). This ensures $q_0=0$ and it can always be arranged by modification of $\rho,$ if necessary.
nodes.statement_short: Along a Peano curve $\rho$ filling the disk, $q_t$ is the Haagerup-Schultz projection of $\rho([0,t])$; $\mathcal{D}$, $\mathcal{D}_n$ are the algebras they generate.
nodes.label: peano

nodes.name: Modulus of continuity of $\rho$
nodes.statement: Since the function $\rho$ is uniformly continuous, it follows that there exists a monotone function $\omega:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}_+$ (called the modulus of continuity of $\rho$) such that $\omega(+0)=0$ and such that $$|\rho(t_1)-\rho(t_2)|\leq\omega(|t_1-t_2|),\quad t_1,t_2\in[0,1].$$

nodes.name: Norm convergence of ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$
nodes.statement: Let $T\in\mathcal{M}$ and let $q_t$, $\mathcal{D}$ and $\mathcal{D}_n$ be as in Construction \ref{peano}. Then ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ converges in norm to ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$, and, in fact, we have $$\|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)\|_{\infty}\le\omega(2^{-n}),$$ where $\omega$ is the modulus of continuity of $\rho.$
assumptions: Let $T\in\mathcal{M}$ and let $q_t$, $\mathcal{D}$ and $\mathcal{D}_n$ be as in Construction \ref{peano}.
conclusions: ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ converges in norm to ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$
nodes.statement_short: ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)\to{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ in norm, with error at most $\omega(2^{-n})$.

nodes.statement: Let $T\in\mathcal{M}$, $\mathcal{D}$ and $\mathcal{D}_n$ be as in Construction \ref{peano}. The Brown measure of the normal operator ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ equals that of $T.$

nodes.name: Compressing to the block diagonal is log-submajorized
nodes.statement: Let $T\in\mathcal{M}$ and let $p\in\mathcal{M}$ be a projection such that $Tp=pTp.$ Then $$Tp+(1-p)T\prec\prec_{\log}T.$$
assumptions: Let $T\in\mathcal{M}$ and let $p\in\mathcal{M}$ be a projection such that $Tp=pTp.$
nodes.label: lem:anytrace

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 18
nodes.statement: Let $S=Tp+(1-p)T.$ Writing elements of $\mathcal{M}$ as matrices with respect to projections $p$ and $(1-p),$ we have $$T=\left(\begin{matrix}A&B\\0&C\end{matrix}\right),\qquad S=\left(\begin{matrix}A&0\\0&C\end{matrix}\right),$$ with $A=Tp$ and $C=(1-p)T.$ By Lemma~\ref{boolean lemma}, there exist increasing nets $p_s\le p,$ $0\leq s\leq\tau(p),$ and $q_s\le 1-p,$ $0\leq s\leq\tau(1-p),$ of projections in $\mathcal{M}$ such that $\tau(p_s)=s$, $\tau(q_s)=s$ and such that $$|C|=\int_0^{\tau({\rm supp}(C))}\mu(s,C)dq_s,\quad |A^*|=\int_0^{\tau({\rm supp}(A))}\mu(s,A)dp_s.$$ Choosing appropriate spectral projections of $A$ and $C$, we see that for every $t>0,$ there exist $t_1,t_2>0$ such that $t_1+t_2=t$ and such that \begin{equation} \int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S))ds=\int_0^{t_1}\log(\mu(s,A))ds+\int_0^{t_2}\log(\mu(s,C))ds. \end{equation} Set $$A_0=\int_0^{t_1}\mu(s,A)dp_s,\quad C_0=\int_0^{t_2}\mu(s,C)dq_s$$ and $$T_0=\begin{pmatrix} A_0&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix},\quad S_0=\begin{pmatrix} A_0&0\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}.$$ Note that $$\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S))ds=\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S_0))ds.$$ We now claim that $\mu(T_0)\leq\mu(T).$ Indeed, $$\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C \end{pmatrix}^*\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C \end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix} A^*A&A^*B\\ B^*A&B^*B+C^*C \end{pmatrix}\geq\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}^*\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}$$ and $$\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}^*=\begin{pmatrix} AA^*+BB^*&BC_0\\ C_0B&C_0^2 \end{pmatrix}\geq\begin{pmatrix} A_0&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} A_0&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}^*.$$ Therefore, $$\mu(T)=\mu(\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C \end{pmatrix})\geq \mu(\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix})\geq\mu(\begin{pmatrix} A_0&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix})=\mu(T_0).$$ Let now $r=p_{\tau({\rm supp}(C_0))}+q_{\tau({\rm supp}(A_0))}.$ Using~\eqref{det}, we get $$\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S))ds=\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S_0))ds=\log(\Delta_{r\mathcal{M}r}(S_0))$$ and, since $\mu(rT_0r)\le\mu(T_0)\le\mu(T)$, we get $$\log(\Delta_{r\mathcal{M}r}(rT_0r))\stackrel{\eqref{det}}{=}\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,rT_0r))ds\leq \int_0^t\log(\mu(s,T))ds.$$ It follows now from Theorem~\ref{thm:det nu matrix} that $\Delta_{r\mathcal{M}r}(S_0)=\Delta_{r\mathcal{M}r}(rT_0r)$ and, therefore, $$\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S))ds\leq\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,T))ds.$$
nodes.statement_short: Truncate the diagonal blocks to their top singular values, show $\mu(T_0)\le\mu(T)$ by operator inequalities, and compare Fuglede-Kadison determinants via Theorem 10.

nodes.name: Determinant inequality for the block-diagonal part
nodes.statement: Let $T\in\mathcal{M}$ and let $p\in\mathcal{M}$ be a projection such that $Tp=pTp.$ Then $$\Delta(1+\big|Tp+(1-p)T)\big|^2)\le\Delta(1+|T|^2).$$
assumptions: Let $T\in\mathcal{M}$ and let $p\in\mathcal{M}$ be a projection such that $Tp=pTp.$
nodes.label: standard

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 19
nodes.statement: Set $y=\mu(Tp+(1-p)T)$ and $x=\mu(T).$ We may without loss of generality assume $y$ is not identically $0.$ By Lemma \ref{lem:anytrace}, we have $y\prec\prec_{\log}x.$ Set $\alpha$ to be the infimum of the set $y^{-1}(\{0\}).$ Then we must have $\inf x^{-1}(\{0\})\ge\alpha.$ Let $\varepsilon_n=\min\{y(\alpha-\frac1n),x(\alpha-\frac1n)\}$ for all integers $n$ so large that $\frac1n<\alpha.$ Then the functions $$y_n=\log(\varepsilon_n^{-1}y)\chi_{(0,\alpha-1/n)},\quad x_n=\log(\varepsilon_n^{-1}x)\chi_{(0,\alpha-1/n)},$$ when nonzero, take only values $\ge0.$ Clearly, $y_n\prec\prec x_n.$ Since the function $\Phi_n:z\to\log(1+\varepsilon_n^2e^{2z})$ is convex on $[0,\infty),$ it follows from Theorem \ref{hlp theorem} that \begin{multline*} \int_0^{\alpha-1/n}\log(1+y^2(s))ds=\int_0^1\Phi_n(y_n(s))ds-(1-\alpha+\frac1n)\log(1+\varepsilon_n^2)\\ \leq\int_0^{\alpha-1/n}\Phi_n(x_n(s))ds-(1-\alpha+\frac1n)\log(1+\varepsilon_n^2)=\int_0^{\alpha-1/n}\log(1+x^2(s))ds. \end{multline*} Letting $n\to\infty,$ we obtain \begin{multline*} \int_0^1\log(1+y^2(s))ds=\int_0^{\alpha}\log(1+y^2(s))ds \\ \leq\int_0^{\alpha}\log(1+x^2(s))ds\leq\int_0^1\log(1+x^2(s))ds. \end{multline*} Now \eqref{det} finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: From log-submajorization (Lemma 18), shift to nonnegative functions and apply Hardy-Littlewood-Polya with the convex $\log(1+\varepsilon^2e^{2z})$, then let $n\to\infty$.

Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers and let $\mathcal{D}_n$ be the von Neumann subalgebra generated by $p_{k/2^n},$ $0\leq k\leq 2^n.$ If $T\in\mathcal{M}$ and $Tp_t=p_tTp_t$ for all $t\in[0,1]$, then $$\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)\geq \Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_{n+1}'}(T)|^2+\frac1m).$$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 21
nodes.statement: We let $f_n^k=p_{(k+1)/2^n}-p_{k/2^n},$ $0\leq k<2^n$ and similarly $f_{n+1}^k=p_{(k+1)/2^{n+1}}-p_{k/2^{n+1}},$ $0\leq k<2^{n+1}$ . For an arbitrary $X\in\mathcal{M}$, we have \[ {\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(X)=\sum_{k=0}^{2^n-1}f_n^kXf_n^k,\qquad {\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_{n+1}'}(X)=\sum_{k=0}^{2^{n+1}-1}f_{n+1}^kXf_{n+1}^k. \] Note that $T$ is upper--triangular with respect to the list of projections $(f_n^k)_{0\le k<2^n}$ and $(f_{n+1}^k)_{0\le k<2^{n+1}}$ and, in particular, $f_{n+1}^{2k}$ is $f_n^kTf_n^k$-invariant and we may write $$f_n^kTf_n^k=\begin{pmatrix} f_{n+1}^{2k+1}Tf_{n+1}^{2k+1}&f_{n+1}^{2k}Tf_{n+1}^{2k+1}\\ 0&f_{n+1}^{2k}Tf_{n+1}^{2k} \end{pmatrix}.$$ It follows from Corollary \ref{standard} and Theorem~\ref{thm:det nu matrix} that \begin{multline*} \Delta_{f_{n+1}^{2k+1}\mathcal{M}f_{n+1}^{2k+1}}(|f_{n+1}^{2k+1}Tf_{n+1}^{2k+1}|^2+\frac1m)^{\tau(f_{n+1}^{2k+1})}\Delta_{f_{n+1}^{2k}\mathcal{M}f_{n+1}^{2k}}(|f_{n+1}^{2k}Tf_{n+1}^{2k}|^2+\frac1m)^{\tau(f_{n+1}^{2k})} \\ \leq\Delta_{f_n^k\mathcal{M}f_n^k}(|f_n^kTf_n^k|^2+\frac1m)^{\tau(f^k_n)}. \end{multline*} It follows now from Theorem~\ref{thm:det nu matrix} that \begin{multline*} \Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)=\prod_{k=0}^{2^n-1}\Delta_{f_n^k\mathcal{M}f_n^k}(|f_n^kTf_n^k|^2+\frac1m)^{\tau(f^k_n)} \\ \geq\prod_{k=0}^{2^{n+1}-1}\Delta_{f_{n+1}^k\mathcal{M}f_{n+1}^k}(|f_{n+1}^kTf_{n+1}^k|^2+\frac1m)^{\tau(f^k_{n+1})}=\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_{n+1}'}(T)|^2+\frac1m) \end{multline*}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 22
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{D}_n$ be the algebra generated by the projections $p_{k/2^n},$ $0\leq k\leq 2^n$. Using the continuity from the right of $p_t$, we get $\mathcal{D}'=\bigcap_{n\geq1}\mathcal{D}_n'$ and, by Lemma \ref{exp limit lemma}, we have $${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)=\lim_{n\to\infty}{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)$$ in the strong operator topology. By Lemma \ref{vspom lemma}, the quantity $\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)$ is decreasing in $n$ and it is, trivially, also decreasing in $m.$ It follows from Lemma \ref{monotone triv} that \begin{equation} \lim_{n\to\infty}\lim_{m\to\infty}\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)=\lim_{m\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m). \end{equation} Note that, by $T$-invariance of the projections $p_{k/2^n}$, using them to write $T$ as a block matrix of operators, yields an upper triangular matrix, and ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)$ is obtained by setting the non-diagonal blocks to zero. To compute the left hand side of \eqref{first exp}, Theorem \ref{thm:det nu matrix} yields $\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T))=\Delta(T)$ and, thereby, we have $$\lim_{m\to\infty}\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)=2\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T))=2\Delta(T).$$ Letting $n\to\infty,$ we infer that the left hand side of \eqref{first exp} is $2\Delta(T)$. To compute the right hand side of \eqref{first exp}, by Lemma 2.25 of \cite{HS1}, we have $$\lim_{n\to\infty}\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)=\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)|^2+\frac1m).$$ Letting $m\to\infty,$ we infer that the right hand side of \eqref{first exp} is $2\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)).$ Thus, we have~\eqref{eq:DeltaD'T}.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 23
nodes.statement: The operator $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ when written as a matrix with respect to the nonzero projections from the list $(f^n_k)_{k=0}^{2^n-1}$ is upper triangular by Theorem \ref{thm:HS} \eqref{hsb} and has for diagonal entries \begin{equation} f^n_kTf^n_k-\frac{\tau(f^n_kTf^n_k)}{\tau(f^n_k)}f^n_k. \end{equation} Repeating the argument in Lemma \ref{lem:Enormconv} (see \eqref{trace partitioning}), we obtain, when $f^n_k\ne0$, that the Brown measure of $f^n_kTf^n_k$ in $f^n_k\mathcal{M}f^n_k$ is supported in $\rho((\frac{k}{2^n},\frac{k+1}{2^n}])$ and $\tau(f^n_kTf^n_k)/\tau(f^n_k)$ lies in the convex hull of this set. Hence, the Brown measure of the difference \eqref{eq:fkdiagelt} is supported in the ball centered at the origin of radius $\operatorname{diam}(\rho((\frac{k}{2^n},\frac {k+1}{2^n}]))$, which is no greater than $\omega(2^{-n}).$ Now applying Theorem \ref{thm:det nu matrix} $n$ times, we get that the Brown measure of $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ lies in the ball of radius $\omega(2^{-n})$ centered at the origin.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 24
nodes.statement: We assume without loss of generality $\|T\|_{\infty}\leq 1/2$. For every $n\geq0,$ let $\mathcal{D}_n$ be the subalgebra of $\mathcal{D}$ generated by $q_{k/2^n}$, $0\leq k\leq 2^n$. Fix $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and a unit vector $\eta\in H.$ By assumption, $T$ commutes with ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T).$ Since $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ and ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ commute, we have $$(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T))^{2m}=\sum_{k=0}^{2m}(-1)^k\binom{2m}{k}({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^{2m-k}(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^k.$$ Since $\|T\|_{\infty}\leq 1/2,$ it follows that both ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ and $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ are contractions. For $k\leq m,$ we have $$\|({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^{2m-k}(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^k\eta\|\leq\|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)\|_{\infty}^m.$$ For $k>m,$ we have $$\|({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^{2m-k}(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^k\eta\|\leq\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^m\eta\|.$$ Hence, by Lemma \ref{lem:Enormconv}, we have \begin{equation} \|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T))^{2m}\eta\|\leq 2^{2m}\max\{\omega(2^{-n})^m,\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^m\eta\|\}. \end{equation} By Lemma \ref{brown small bound}, the Brown measure of $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ is contained in the ball of radius $\omega(2^{-n})$ centered at $0.$ By the Haagerup--Schultz characterization \eqref{eq:H-S H_r}, for every unit vector $\xi\in H,$ there exists a sequence $\xi_m\to\xi$ such that $\|\xi_m\|=1$ and $$\limsup_{m\to\infty}\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^m\xi_m\|^{1/m}\leq\omega(2^{-n}).$$ Hence, there exists $M$ (depending on $n$), such that $$\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^m\xi_m\|\leq (2\omega(2^{-n}))^m,\quad m>M.$$ Substituting $\xi_m$ for $\eta$ in \eqref{eq:TEpow}, we obtain $$\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T))^{2m}\xi_m\|^{1/m}\leq 8\omega(2^{-n}),\quad m>M.$$ Since $\xi$ was any unit vector, it follows from the characterization \eqref{eq:H-S H_r} of the Haagerup--Schultz subspace that the Brown measure of $(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T))^2$ is supported in the ball centered at $0$ of radius $8\omega(2^{-n}).$ Letting $n\to\infty,$ we obtain that the Brown measure of $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ is $\delta_0.$
nodes.statement_short: Binomial expansion of $(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T))^{2m}$ using commutativity, bounded via Lemmas 15 and 23. The key step uses the Haagerup-Schultz subspace characterization to bound the Brown measure radius by $8\omega(2^{-n})$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6
nodes.statement: Let $q_t,$ $t\in[0,1],$ and $\mathcal{D}$ be as in Construction \ref{peano}. Applying Lemma \ref{first exp lemma} to the operators $Tq_t-\lambda$ and $(1-q_t)T-\lambda,$ we obtain \begin{align*} \Delta(Tq_t-\lambda)&=\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D'}}(Tq_t)-\lambda), \\ \Delta((1-q_t)T-\lambda)&=\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}((1-q_t)T-\lambda)). \end{align*} Hence, by \eqref{br def}, the Brown measure of the operator $Tq_t$ (respectively, of $(1-q_t)T$) equals that of ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)q_t$ (respectively, of $(1-q_t){\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)$). In particular, the projection $q_t$ is the Haagerup--Schultz projection for ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)$ associated to the set $\rho([0,t]).$ By definition of $\mathcal{D}',$ the operator ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D'}}(T)$ commutes with every $q_t.$ Hence, ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)$ satisfies the hypotheses of Lemma \ref{comm quasinilpotent}. Since $\mathcal{D}\subseteq\mathcal{D}'$ we have ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T))={\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ and by application of this lemma we infer that the Brown measure of the operator ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D'}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ is $\delta_0.$ Applying Lemma \ref{first exp lemma} to the operator $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-\lambda,$ we obtain $$\Delta(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-\lambda)=\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D'}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-\lambda).$$ Hence, by \eqref{br def}, the Brown measure of the operator $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ equals that of ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D'}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$, i.e., it is $\delta_0$. Now letting $Q=T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ and $N={\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$, we have $T=N+Q$ with $N$ normal and $Q$ s.o.t.-quasinilpotent. This proves Theorem \ref{decomposition} \eqref{decc}. Theorem \ref{decomposition} \eqref{decb} is already proved in Proposition \ref{br equ}.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 25
nodes.statement: We prove the if part first. For a given $u\in(0,1),$ set $t=\mu(u,A).$ We have $$\int_0^u\log(\frac{\mu(s,B)}{t})ds\leq\tau(\log_+(\frac{|B|}{t}))\leq\tau(\log_+(\frac{|A|}{t}))=\int_0^u\log(\frac{\mu(s,A)}{t})ds.$$ Hence, $B\prec\prec_{\log}A.$ We now prove the only if part. nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 26
nodes.statement: By enlarging $\mathcal{M}$ if necessary, we may without loss of generality assume it is diffuse. Referring to Lemma \ref{boolean lemma}, we infer the existence of increasing nets $p_s,q_s$ $0\leq s\leq1,$ of projections in $\mathcal{M}$ such that $\tau(p_s)=s,$ $\tau(q_s)=s$ and such that $$B=\int_0^1\mu(s,B)dq_s,\quad A=\int_0^1\mu(s,A)dp_s.$$ Fix $t<\tau({\rm supp}(B))$ and define the operators $$B_t=\int_0^t\mu(s,B)dq_s,\quad C_t=\int_0^t\mu(s,B)dp_s,\quad A_t=\int_0^t\mu(s,A)dp_s.$$ It is clear that $\mu(B_t)=\mu(C_t),$ $C_t\prec\prec_{\log} A_t$ and the operators $A_t,C_t$ are in the von Neumann algebra $p_t\mathcal{M}p_t$. Note that we have $\tau({\rm supp}(B_t))=\tau({\rm supp}(C_t))\le\tau({\rm supp}(A_t))$. Since $t<\tau({\rm supp}(B)),$ it follows that $A_t$ and $C_t$ are invertible and $\log(A_t),\log(C_t)\in p_t\mathcal{M}p_t$. Let $r=\max\{\|A_t^{-1}\|_{\infty},\|C_t^{-1}\|_{\infty}\}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:log invertibles}, from $C_t\prec\prec_{\log}A_t$ we get $rC_t\prec\prec_{\log}rA_t$ and $\log(r C_t)\prec\prec\log(rA_t)$. Since the mapping $\Phi:z\to\log(1+r^{-1}e^z)$ is convex, it follows from Theorem \ref{hlp theorem} that \[ \int_0^t\log(1+\mu(s,B))ds=\tau(\Phi(\log(rC_t)))\leq\tau(\Phi(\log(rA_t)))=\int_0^t\log(1+\mu(s,A))ds. \] Since $t<\tau({\rm supp}(B))$ is arbitrary, the assertion follows.

nodes.statement: Letting $f^n_k$ be as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:Enormconv} and using~\eqref{eq:EDn}, we have \begin{equation} \log\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)-\lambda|^2+\varepsilon)=\sum_{\substack{0\le k<2^n \\ f^n_k\ne0}}\tau(f^n_k)\log(|\frac{\tau(f^n_kTf^n_k)}{\tau(f^n_k)}-\lambda|^2+\varepsilon). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Rewrite as an integral of $x_n$ against $\nu_T$
nodes.statement: By Theorem \ref{thm:HS}, we have $\tau(f^n_k)=\nu_T(\rho([0,\frac{k+1}{2^n}])\backslash \rho([0,\frac{k}{2^n}])).$ Hence, using~\eqref{eq:logEDn}, we get \begin{equation} \log\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)-\lambda|^2+\varepsilon)=\int_{\{|z|\leq\|T\|_{\infty}\}}x_n(z)d\nu_T(z). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Uniform bound on $x_n$
nodes.statement: Moreover, we clearly have $$\log(\varepsilon)\leq x_n(z)\leq \log(\varepsilon+(|\lambda|+\|T\|_{\infty})^2) $$ for every $|z|\le\|T\|_\infty$ and, therefore, $$\|x_n\|_{\infty}\leq\max\{|\log(\varepsilon)|,|\log(\varepsilon+(|\lambda|+\|T\|_{\infty})^2)|\}.$$

nodes.name: Distance of $z$ to the block average
nodes.statement: Given $z\in\rho([0,\frac{k+1}{2^n}])\backslash \rho([0,\frac{k}{2^n}])$ with $\tau(f^n_k)\ne0$, by Theorem \ref{thm:HS} \eqref{hsc},\eqref{hsd} combined with Brown's version of Lidskii theorem \cite{Brown}, we have $$\frac{\tau(f^n_kTf^n_k)}{\tau(f^n_k)}\in\overline{\rm conv}(\rho([0,\frac{k+1}{2^n}])\backslash \rho([0,\frac{k}{2^n}]))\subset\overline{\rm conv}(\rho((\frac{k}{2^n},\frac{k+1}{2^n}])).$$ Thus, \begin{equation} |z-\frac{\tau(f^n_kTf^n_k)}{\tau(f^n_k)}|\leq{\rm diam}(\rho((\frac{k}{2^n},\frac{k+1}{2^n}])))\leq\omega(2^{-n}). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Distance of $z$ to the block average

nodes.name: Pointwise convergence and dominated convergence
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{ccckkk} and \eqref{xn def}, we infer that $x_n(z)$ converges to $\log(|z-\lambda|^2+\varepsilon)$ as $n\to\infty$ on a set of full $\nu_T$ measure. The Dominated Convergence Principle now yields that the right-hand-side of~\eqref{tttkkk} tends to the right-hand-side of~\eqref{eq:det convergence} as $n\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Norm convergence and continuity of the determinant
nodes.statement: Fix $\varepsilon>0.$ By Lemma \ref{lem:Enormconv}, we have that ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ converges in norm to ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ as $n\to\infty.$ Since the Fuglede-Kadison determinant is continuous with respect to the uniform norm topology on the set of invertible elements (see~\cite{FK}), for every $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}$ we have $$\log\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)-\lambda|^2+\varepsilon)\to\log(\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-\lambda|^2+\varepsilon)).$$
nodes.statement_short: Norm convergence and continuity of the determinant

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 16 and identify limits
nodes.statement: On the other hand, it follows from Lemma \ref{det convergence} that $$\log\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)-\lambda|^2+\varepsilon)\to\int_{\mathbb{C}}\log(|z-\lambda|^2+\varepsilon)d\nu_T(z)$$ for every $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}.$ Hence, $$\log(\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-\lambda|^2+\varepsilon))=\int_{\mathbb{C}}\log(|z-\lambda|^2+\varepsilon)d\nu_T(z)$$ for every $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}.$

nodes.name: Monotone convergence as $\varepsilon\to0$
nodes.statement: Letting $\varepsilon\to0,$ we infer from the Monotone Convergence Principle that $$\int_{\mathbb{C}}\log(|z-\lambda|)d\nu_{{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)}(z)=\int_{\mathbb{C}}\log(|z-\lambda|)d\nu_T(z)$$ for every $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}.$

nodes.name: Take Laplacians
nodes.statement: The assertion follows by taking Laplacians of both sides.

nodes.name: Block matrix form of $T$ and $S$
nodes.statement: Let $S=Tp+(1-p)T.$ Writing elements of $\mathcal{M}$ as matrices with respect to projections $p$ and $(1-p),$ we have $$T=\left(\begin{matrix}A&B\\0&C\end{matrix}\right),\qquad S=\left(\begin{matrix}A&0\\0&C\end{matrix}\right),$$ with $A=Tp$ and $C=(1-p)T.$

nodes.name: Spectral nests for $|C|$ and $|A^*|$ from Lemma 9
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{boolean lemma}, there exist increasing nets $p_s\le p,$ $0\leq s\leq\tau(p),$ and $q_s\le 1-p,$ $0\leq s\leq\tau(1-p),$ of projections in $\mathcal{M}$ such that $\tau(p_s)=s$, $\tau(q_s)=s$ and such that $$|C|=\int_0^{\tau({\rm supp}(C))}\mu(s,C)dq_s,\quad |A^*|=\int_0^{\tau({\rm supp}(A))}\mu(s,A)dp_s.$$
nodes.statement_short: Spectral nests for $|C|$ and $|A^*|$ from Lemma 9

nodes.name: Split the log-integral of $\mu(S)$
nodes.statement: Choosing appropriate spectral projections of $A$ and $C$, we see that for every $t>0,$ there exist $t_1,t_2>0$ such that $t_1+t_2=t$ and such that \begin{equation} \int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S))ds=\int_0^{t_1}\log(\mu(s,A))ds+\int_0^{t_2}\log(\mu(s,C))ds. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Truncated operators $A_0,C_0,T_0,S_0$
nodes.statement: Set $$A_0=\int_0^{t_1}\mu(s,A)dp_s,\quad C_0=\int_0^{t_2}\mu(s,C)dq_s$$ and $$T_0=\begin{pmatrix} A_0&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix},\quad S_0=\begin{pmatrix} A_0&0\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}.$$ Note that $$\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S))ds=\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S_0))ds.$$

nodes.name: Claim $\mu(T_0)\le\mu(T)$
nodes.statement: We now claim that $\mu(T_0)\leq\mu(T).$ Indeed, $$\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C \end{pmatrix}^*\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C \end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix} A^*A&A^*B\\ B^*A&B^*B+C^*C \end{pmatrix}\geq\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}^*\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}$$ and $$\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}^*=\begin{pmatrix} AA^*+BB^*&BC_0\\ C_0B&C_0^2 \end{pmatrix}\geq\begin{pmatrix} A_0&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} A_0&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}^*.$$ Therefore, $$\mu(T)=\mu(\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C \end{pmatrix})\geq \mu(\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix})\geq\mu(\begin{pmatrix} A_0&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix})=\mu(T_0).$$

nodes.name: Operator inequalities for the products
nodes.statement: Indeed, $$\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C \end{pmatrix}^*\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C \end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix} A^*A&A^*B\\ B^*A&B^*B+C^*C \end{pmatrix}\geq\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}^*\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}$$ and $$\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}^*=\begin{pmatrix} AA^*+BB^*&BC_0\\ C_0B&C_0^2 \end{pmatrix}\geq\begin{pmatrix} A_0&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} A_0&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}^*.$$

nodes.name: Conclude the claim
nodes.statement: Therefore, $$\mu(T)=\mu(\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C \end{pmatrix})\geq \mu(\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix})\geq\mu(\begin{pmatrix} A_0&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix})=\mu(T_0).$$

nodes.name: Compare determinants in $r\mathcal{M}r$
nodes.statement: Let now $r=p_{\tau({\rm supp}(C_0))}+q_{\tau({\rm supp}(A_0))}.$ Using~\eqref{det}, we get $$\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S))ds=\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S_0))ds=\log(\Delta_{r\mathcal{M}r}(S_0))$$ and, since $\mu(rT_0r)\le\mu(T_0)\le\mu(T)$, we get $$\log(\Delta_{r\mathcal{M}r}(rT_0r))\stackrel{\eqref{det}}{=}\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,rT_0r))ds\leq \int_0^t\log(\mu(s,T))ds.$$

nodes.name: Conclude via Theorem 10
nodes.statement: It follows now from Theorem~\ref{thm:det nu matrix} that $\Delta_{r\mathcal{M}r}(S_0)=\Delta_{r\mathcal{M}r}(rT_0r)$ and, therefore, $$\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S))ds\leq\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,T))ds.$$

nodes.name: Set $y,x$
nodes.statement: Set $y=\mu(Tp+(1-p)T)$ and $x=\mu(T).$ We may without loss of generality assume $y$ is not identically $0.$

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 18
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lem:anytrace}, we have $y\prec\prec_{\log}x.$

nodes.name: Define $\alpha$
nodes.statement: Set $\alpha$ to be the infimum of the set $y^{-1}(\{0\}).$ Then we must have $\inf x^{-1}(\{0\})\ge\alpha.$

nodes.name: Shifted log functions $y_n,x_n$
nodes.statement: Let $\varepsilon_n=\min\{y(\alpha-\frac1n),x(\alpha-\frac1n)\}$ for all integers $n$ so large that $\frac1n<\alpha.$ Then the functions $$y_n=\log(\varepsilon_n^{-1}y)\chi_{(0,\alpha-1/n)},\quad x_n=\log(\varepsilon_n^{-1}x)\chi_{(0,\alpha-1/n)},$$ when nonzero, take only values $\ge0.$ Clearly, $y_n\prec\prec x_n.$

nodes.name: Apply Hardy-Littlewood-Polya
nodes.statement: Since the function $\Phi_n:z\to\log(1+\varepsilon_n^2e^{2z})$ is convex on $[0,\infty),$ it follows from Theorem \ref{hlp theorem} that \begin{multline*} \int_0^{\alpha-1/n}\log(1+y^2(s))ds=\int_0^1\Phi_n(y_n(s))ds-(1-\alpha+\frac1n)\log(1+\varepsilon_n^2)\\ \leq\int_0^{\alpha-1/n}\Phi_n(x_n(s))ds-(1-\alpha+\frac1n)\log(1+\varepsilon_n^2)=\int_0^{\alpha-1/n}\log(1+x^2(s))ds. \end{multline*}

nodes.name: Let $n\to\infty$ and use (2)
nodes.statement: Letting $n\to\infty,$ we obtain \begin{multline*} \int_0^1\log(1+y^2(s))ds=\int_0^{\alpha}\log(1+y^2(s))ds \\ \leq\int_0^{\alpha}\log(1+x^2(s))ds\leq\int_0^1\log(1+x^2(s))ds. \end{multline*} Now \eqref{det} finishes the proof.

nodes.name: Increments and formulas for the expectations
nodes.statement: We let $f_n^k=p_{(k+1)/2^n}-p_{k/2^n},$ $0\leq k<2^n$ and similarly $f_{n+1}^k=p_{(k+1)/2^{n+1}}-p_{k/2^{n+1}},$ $0\leq k<2^{n+1}$ . For an arbitrary $X\in\mathcal{M}$, we have \[ {\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(X)=\sum_{k=0}^{2^n-1}f_n^kXf_n^k,\qquad {\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_{n+1}'}(X)=\sum_{k=0}^{2^{n+1}-1}f_{n+1}^kXf_{n+1}^k. \]
nodes.statement_short: Increments and formulas for the expectations

nodes.name: Write each block as $2\times2$ upper triangular
nodes.statement: Note that $T$ is upper--triangular with respect to the list of projections $(f_n^k)_{0\le k<2^n}$ and $(f_{n+1}^k)_{0\le k<2^{n+1}}$ and, in particular, $f_{n+1}^{2k}$ is $f_n^kTf_n^k$-invariant and we may write $$f_n^kTf_n^k=\begin{pmatrix} f_{n+1}^{2k+1}Tf_{n+1}^{2k+1}&f_{n+1}^{2k}Tf_{n+1}^{2k+1}\\ 0&f_{n+1}^{2k}Tf_{n+1}^{2k} \end{pmatrix}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Write each block as $2\times2$ upper triangular

nodes.name: Apply Corollary 19 and Theorem 10 blockwise
nodes.statement: It follows from Corollary \ref{standard} and Theorem~\ref{thm:det nu matrix} that \begin{multline*} \Delta_{f_{n+1}^{2k+1}\mathcal{M}f_{n+1}^{2k+1}}(|f_{n+1}^{2k+1}Tf_{n+1}^{2k+1}|^2+\frac1m)^{\tau(f_{n+1}^{2k+1})}\Delta_{f_{n+1}^{2k}\mathcal{M}f_{n+1}^{2k}}(|f_{n+1}^{2k}Tf_{n+1}^{2k}|^2+\frac1m)^{\tau(f_{n+1}^{2k})} \\ \leq\Delta_{f_n^k\mathcal{M}f_n^k}(|f_n^kTf_n^k|^2+\frac1m)^{\tau(f^k_n)}. \end{multline*}

nodes.name: Multiply over blocks
nodes.statement: It follows now from Theorem~\ref{thm:det nu matrix} that \begin{multline*} \Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)=\prod_{k=0}^{2^n-1}\Delta_{f_n^k\mathcal{M}f_n^k}(|f_n^kTf_n^k|^2+\frac1m)^{\tau(f^k_n)} \\ \geq\prod_{k=0}^{2^{n+1}-1}\Delta_{f_{n+1}^k\mathcal{M}f_{n+1}^k}(|f_{n+1}^kTf_{n+1}^k|^2+\frac1m)^{\tau(f^k_{n+1})}=\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_{n+1}'}(T)|^2+\frac1m) \end{multline*}

nodes.name: Strong convergence of expectations (Lemma 13)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{D}_n$ be the algebra generated by the projections $p_{k/2^n},$ $0\leq k\leq 2^n$. Using the continuity from the right of $p_t$, we get $\mathcal{D}'=\bigcap_{n\geq1}\mathcal{D}_n'$ and, by Lemma \ref{exp limit lemma}, we have $${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)=\lim_{n\to\infty}{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)$$ in the strong operator topology.

nodes.name: Monotonicity and interchange of limits
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{vspom lemma}, the quantity $\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)$ is decreasing in $n$ and it is, trivially, also decreasing in $m.$ It follows from Lemma \ref{monotone triv} that \begin{equation} \lim_{n\to\infty}\lim_{m\to\infty}\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)=\lim_{m\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Evaluate the left-hand side
nodes.statement: Note that, by $T$-invariance of the projections $p_{k/2^n}$, using them to write $T$ as a block matrix of operators, yields an upper triangular matrix, and ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)$ is obtained by setting the non-diagonal blocks to zero. To compute the left hand side of \eqref{first exp}, Theorem \ref{thm:det nu matrix} yields $\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T))=\Delta(T)$ and, thereby, we have $$\lim_{m\to\infty}\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)=2\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T))=2\Delta(T).$$ Letting $n\to\infty,$ we infer that the left hand side of \eqref{first exp} is $2\Delta(T)$.

nodes.name: Evaluate the right-hand side via [HS1]
nodes.statement: To compute the right hand side of \eqref{first exp}, by Lemma 2.25 of \cite{HS1}, we have $$\lim_{n\to\infty}\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)=\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)|^2+\frac1m).$$ Letting $m\to\infty,$ we infer that the right hand side of \eqref{first exp} is $2\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)).$

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Thus, we have~\eqref{eq:DeltaD'T}.

nodes.name: Upper triangular form and diagonal entries
nodes.statement: The operator $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ when written as a matrix with respect to the nonzero projections from the list $(f^n_k)_{k=0}^{2^n-1}$ is upper triangular by Theorem \ref{thm:HS} \eqref{hsb} and has for diagonal entries \begin{equation} f^n_kTf^n_k-\frac{\tau(f^n_kTf^n_k)}{\tau(f^n_k)}f^n_k. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Upper triangular form and diagonal entries

nodes.name: Locate block Brown measures
nodes.statement: Repeating the argument in Lemma \ref{lem:Enormconv} (see \eqref{trace partitioning}), we obtain, when $f^n_k\ne0$, that the Brown measure of $f^n_kTf^n_k$ in $f^n_k\mathcal{M}f^n_k$ is supported in $\rho((\frac{k}{2^n},\frac{k+1}{2^n}])$ and $\tau(f^n_kTf^n_k)/\tau(f^n_k)$ lies in the convex hull of this set.

nodes.name: Each diagonal block has small Brown measure
nodes.statement: Hence, the Brown measure of the difference \eqref{eq:fkdiagelt} is supported in the ball centered at the origin of radius $\operatorname{diam}(\rho((\frac{k}{2^n},\frac {k+1}{2^n}]))$, which is no greater than $\omega(2^{-n}).$
nodes.statement_short: Each diagonal block has small Brown measure

nodes.name: Combine by Theorem 10
nodes.statement: Now applying Theorem \ref{thm:det nu matrix} $n$ times, we get that the Brown measure of $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ lies in the ball of radius $\omega(2^{-n})$ centered at the origin.

nodes.name: WLOG $\|T\|\le1/2$
nodes.statement: We assume without loss of generality $\|T\|_{\infty}\leq 1/2$.

nodes.name: Fix $n$ and $\eta$
nodes.statement: For every $n\geq0,$ let $\mathcal{D}_n$ be the subalgebra of $\mathcal{D}$ generated by $q_{k/2^n}$, $0\leq k\leq 2^n$. Fix $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and a unit vector $\eta\in H.$

nodes.name: Binomial expansion
nodes.statement: By assumption, $T$ commutes with ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T).$ Since $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ and ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ commute, we have $$(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T))^{2m}=\sum_{k=0}^{2m}(-1)^k\binom{2m}{k}({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^{2m-k}(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^k.$$

nodes.name: Contraction bounds
nodes.statement: Since $\|T\|_{\infty}\leq 1/2,$ it follows that both ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ and $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ are contractions.

nodes.name: Bound the power applied to $\eta$
nodes.statement: For $k\leq m,$ we have $$\|({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^{2m-k}(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^k\eta\|\leq\|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)\|_{\infty}^m.$$ For $k>m,$ we have $$\|({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^{2m-k}(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^k\eta\|\leq\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^m\eta\|.$$ Hence, by Lemma \ref{lem:Enormconv}, we have \begin{equation} \|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T))^{2m}\eta\|\leq 2^{2m}\max\{\omega(2^{-n})^m,\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^m\eta\|\}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Haagerup-Schultz subspace gives vectors with small powers
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{brown small bound}, the Brown measure of $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ is contained in the ball of radius $\omega(2^{-n})$ centered at $0.$ By the Haagerup--Schultz characterization \eqref{eq:H-S H_r}, for every unit vector $\xi\in H,$ there exists a sequence $\xi_m\to\xi$ such that $\|\xi_m\|=1$ and $$\limsup_{m\to\infty}\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^m\xi_m\|^{1/m}\leq\omega(2^{-n}).$$ Hence, there exists $M$ (depending on $n$), such that $$\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^m\xi_m\|\leq (2\omega(2^{-n}))^m,\quad m>M.$$
nodes.statement_short: Haagerup-Schultz subspace gives vectors with small powers

nodes.name: Bound Brown measure of the square
nodes.statement: Substituting $\xi_m$ for $\eta$ in \eqref{eq:TEpow}, we obtain $$\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T))^{2m}\xi_m\|^{1/m}\leq 8\omega(2^{-n}),\quad m>M.$$ Since $\xi$ was any unit vector, it follows from the characterization \eqref{eq:H-S H_r} of the Haagerup--Schultz subspace that the Brown measure of $(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T))^2$ is supported in the ball centered at $0$ of radius $8\omega(2^{-n}).$
nodes.statement_short: Bound Brown measure of the square

nodes.name: Let $n\to\infty$
nodes.statement: Letting $n\to\infty,$ we obtain that the Brown measure of $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ is $\delta_0.$

nodes.name: Lemma 22 matches Brown measures of compressions
nodes.statement: Let $q_t,$ $t\in[0,1],$ and $\mathcal{D}$ be as in Construction \ref{peano}. Applying Lemma \ref{first exp lemma} to the operators $Tq_t-\lambda$ and $(1-q_t)T-\lambda,$ we obtain \begin{align*} \Delta(Tq_t-\lambda)&=\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D'}}(Tq_t)-\lambda), \\ \Delta((1-q_t)T-\lambda)&=\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}((1-q_t)T-\lambda)). \end{align*} Hence, by \eqref{br def}, the Brown measure of the operator $Tq_t$ (respectively, of $(1-q_t)T$) equals that of ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)q_t$ (respectively, of $(1-q_t){\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)$).
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 22 matches Brown measures of compressions

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 24 to ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)$
nodes.statement: In particular, the projection $q_t$ is the Haagerup--Schultz projection for ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)$ associated to the set $\rho([0,t]).$ By definition of $\mathcal{D}',$ the operator ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D'}}(T)$ commutes with every $q_t.$ Hence, ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)$ satisfies the hypotheses of Lemma \ref{comm quasinilpotent}. Since $\mathcal{D}\subseteq\mathcal{D}'$ we have ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T))={\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ and by application of this lemma we infer that the Brown measure of the operator ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D'}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ is $\delta_0.$

nodes.name: Transfer Brown measure to $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$
nodes.statement: Applying Lemma \ref{first exp lemma} to the operator $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-\lambda,$ we obtain $$\Delta(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-\lambda)=\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D'}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-\lambda).$$ Hence, by \eqref{br def}, the Brown measure of the operator $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ equals that of ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D'}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$, i.e., it is $\delta_0$.

nodes.name: Set $N,Q$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Now letting $Q=T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ and $N={\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$, we have $T=N+Q$ with $N$ normal and $Q$ s.o.t.-quasinilpotent. This proves Theorem \ref{decomposition} \eqref{decc}. Theorem \ref{decomposition} \eqref{decb} is already proved in Proposition \ref{br equ}.

nodes.name: The 'if' direction
nodes.statement: We prove the if part first. For a given $u\in(0,1),$ set $t=\mu(u,A).$ We have $$\int_0^u\log(\frac{\mu(s,B)}{t})ds\leq\tau(\log_+(\frac{|B|}{t}))\leq\tau(\log_+(\frac{|A|}{t}))=\int_0^u\log(\frac{\mu(s,A)}{t})ds.$$ Hence, $B\prec\prec_{\log}A.$
nodes.section: 5 A Weyl inequality in the II$_1$--setting

nodes.name: The 'only if' direction
nodes.statement: We now prove the only if part. If $t>\|B\|_{\infty},$ then \eqref{eq:logAtBt} holds trivially, while if $t\le\|B\|_{\infty}$ then we have \begin{multline*} \tau(\log_+(\frac{|B|}{t}))=\int_0^{d_{|B|}(t)}\log(\frac{\mu(s,B)}{t})ds\leq\int_0^{d_{|B|}(t)}\log(\frac{\mu(s,A)}{t})ds \\ \leq\int_0^{d_{|A|}(t)}\log(\frac{\mu(s,A)}{t})ds=\tau(\log_+(\frac{|A|}{t})). \end{multline*}
nodes.section: 5 A Weyl inequality in the II$_1$--setting

nodes.name: WLOG diffuse
nodes.statement: By enlarging $\mathcal{M}$ if necessary, we may without loss of generality assume it is diffuse.
nodes.section: 5 A Weyl inequality in the II$_1$--setting

nodes.name: Spectral nests via Lemma 9
nodes.statement: Referring to Lemma \ref{boolean lemma}, we infer the existence of increasing nets $p_s,q_s$ $0\leq s\leq1,$ of projections in $\mathcal{M}$ such that $\tau(p_s)=s,$ $\tau(q_s)=s$ and such that $$B=\int_0^1\mu(s,B)dq_s,\quad A=\int_0^1\mu(s,A)dp_s.$$
nodes.section: 5 A Weyl inequality in the II$_1$--setting

nodes.name: Truncated operators $B_t,C_t,A_t$
nodes.statement: Fix $t<\tau({\rm supp}(B))$ and define the operators $$B_t=\int_0^t\mu(s,B)dq_s,\quad C_t=\int_0^t\mu(s,B)dp_s,\quad A_t=\int_0^t\mu(s,A)dp_s.$$ It is clear that $\mu(B_t)=\mu(C_t),$ $C_t\prec\prec_{\log} A_t$ and the operators $A_t,C_t$ are in the von Neumann algebra $p_t\mathcal{M}p_t$.
nodes.section: 5 A Weyl inequality in the II$_1$--setting

nodes.name: Invertibility of truncations
nodes.statement: Note that we have $\tau({\rm supp}(B_t))=\tau({\rm supp}(C_t))\le\tau({\rm supp}(A_t))$. Since $t<\tau({\rm supp}(B)),$ it follows that $A_t$ and $C_t$ are invertible and $\log(A_t),\log(C_t)\in p_t\mathcal{M}p_t$.
nodes.section: 5 A Weyl inequality in the II$_1$--setting

nodes.name: Rescale and take logarithms (Lemma 12)
nodes.statement: Let $r=\max\{\|A_t^{-1}\|_{\infty},\|C_t^{-1}\|_{\infty}\}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:log invertibles}, from $C_t\prec\prec_{\log}A_t$ we get $rC_t\prec\prec_{\log}rA_t$ and $\log(r C_t)\prec\prec\log(rA_t)$.
nodes.section: 5 A Weyl inequality in the II$_1$--setting

nodes.name: Apply Hardy-Littlewood-Polya
nodes.statement: Since the mapping $\Phi:z\to\log(1+r^{-1}e^z)$ is convex, it follows from Theorem \ref{hlp theorem} that \[ \int_0^t\log(1+\mu(s,B))ds=\tau(\Phi(\log(rC_t)))\leq\tau(\Phi(\log(rA_t)))=\int_0^t\log(1+\mu(s,A))ds. \]
nodes.section: 5 A Weyl inequality in the II$_1$--setting

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Since $t<\tau({\rm supp}(B))$ is arbitrary, the assertion follows.
nodes.section: 5 A Weyl inequality in the II$_1$--setting

nodes.name: Express $\tau(\log_+(|N|/t))$ via Brown measure of $T$
nodes.statement: Since the Brown measure of $N$ equals the distribution of $N$ and equals the Brown measure of $T$, we have $$\tau(\log_+(\frac{|N|}{t}))=\int_{|z|\geq t}\log(\frac{|z|}{t})d\nu_N(z)=\int_{|z|\geq t}\log(\frac{|z|}{t})d\nu_T(z).$$
nodes.section: 5 A Weyl inequality in the II$_1$--setting

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 2.20 of [HS1]
nodes.statement: It follows from Lemma 2.20 in \cite{HS1} that $$\int_{|z|\geq t}\log(\frac{|z|}{t})d\nu_T(z)\leq\tau(\log_+(\frac{|T|}{t})).$$ Therefore, $$\tau(\log_+(\frac{|N|}{t}))\leq\tau(\log_+(\frac{|T|}{t}))$$
nodes.section: 5 A Weyl inequality in the II$_1$--setting

nodes.name: Part (a) by Lemma 25
nodes.statement: Assertion \eqref{kika} follows now from Lemma \ref{logmaj another}.
nodes.section: 5 A Weyl inequality in the II$_1$--setting

nodes.name: Equality part
nodes.statement: The equality in~\eqref{eq:Weyl} holds since $\mu_T=\mu_N$ and $N$ is normal.
nodes.section: 5 A Weyl inequality in the II$_1$--setting

nodes.name: Lemmas 26 and 12
nodes.statement: Assertion \eqref{kika} together with Lemma \ref{stamp} and homogeneity of logarithmic submajorization shows that $$n|N|+1\prec\prec_{\log}n|T|+1,\quad n\geq1.$$ Now Lemma~\ref{lem:log invertibles} yields $\log(n|N|+1)\prec\prec\log(n|T|+1)$.
nodes.section: 5 A Weyl inequality in the II$_1$--setting

nodes.name: Apply Hardy-Littlewood-Polya
nodes.statement: Since $\Phi\circ\exp$ is convex on $\mathbb{R}$, so is the function $\Phi(\frac1n\exp(\cdot))$ and from Theorem \ref{hlp theorem} we get $$\tau(\Phi(|N|+\frac1n)))\leq\tau(\Phi(|T|+\frac1n))),\quad n\geq 1.$$
nodes.section: 5 A Weyl inequality in the II$_1$--setting

nodes.name: Monotone convergence concludes (b)
nodes.statement: We now infer from the Monotone Convergence Principle that $$\tau(\Phi(|N|))=\lim_{n\to\infty}\tau(\Phi(|N|+\frac1n))\leq\lim_{n\to\infty}\tau(\Phi(|T|+\frac1n))=\tau(\Phi(|T|)).$$ This proves \eqref{kikb}.
